status: drafted via lean single-pass workflow grounded in the real extracted verse text
notes: Verified against this translation's own extracted text (2 chapters, 38 verses: 15+23, matching the stated verse count exactly) — content is verbatim-identical in substance to the KJV Haggai already indexed (same four dated oracles, same two named human addressees, same priestly-ruling episode), so the KJV structure was adapted rather than invented from scratch, with every verse re-checked against this translation's own file. Two named humans beyond the prophet: Zerubbabel (governor) and Joshua son of Josedech (high priest), always addressed together, plus Darius the king as a non-acting dating anchor (kept as a 'named' entry, not folded silently into others). No submanagers - the 'remnant of the people' acts only as an undifferentiated group, cited within the entries it belongs to. Two law/theme tiers split out because each is independently load-bearing: the temple-rebuilding charge (the book's central theme, 1:2-11/2:1-9) and the priests' ceremonial-defilement ruling (2:10-19), a distinct self-contained teaching, not a restatement of the temple charge. NAMING-COLLISION FLAGS carried over and re-verified against this text: this Joshua (son of Josedech) is not Joshua son of Nun; this Darius is conventionally Darius I of Persia but the text itself never distinguishes him from other scriptural Dariuses (Darius the Mede, Darius the Persian) - the identification is external, not textual. All ids suffixed _ethiopian to keep this translation's roster distinct from the existing KJV character set per the project's cross-translation scoping rule.

characters.name: Haggai the prophet

verses.note: In Darius's 2nd year, 6th month, day 1, the word of the LORD comes by Haggai the prophet to Zerubbabel and to Joshua the high priest.
Rebukes the people for dwelling in 'cieled houses' while the LORD's house 'lie[s] waste'; commands them to go to the mountain, bring wood, and build.
The people obey and fear before the LORD; Haggai, called 'the LORD's messenger,' delivers the LORD's reassurance, 'I am with you.'
Second message: encourages the discouraged builders, promises the latter house's glory will exceed the former's, and 'in this place will I give peace.'
At the LORD's instruction, poses two ceremonial-law questions to the priests and applies the answer to the nation's uncleanness.
Delivers the final oracle to Zerubbabel alone, promising he will be made 'as a signet.'

funFacts: Every one of his messages in this text carries an exact date (1:1; 2:1; 2:10; 2:20).

characters.name: Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel

genealogy.note: Called 'the son of Shealtiel' throughout this text (1:1, 1:12, 1:14, 2:2, 2:4, 2:21, 2:23), matching the KJV's own genealogical claim for him.

verses.note: Addressed as 'governor of Judah' alongside Joshua the high priest.
Obeys the voice of the LORD along with Joshua and the remnant of the people.
The LORD stirs up his spirit, and he comes to work on the house of the LORD.
Told directly, 'be strong, O Zerubbabel... and work: for I am with you.'
Final oracle addressed to him alone: 'I will take thee, O Zerubbabel, my servant... and will make thee as a signet: for I have chosen thee.'

funFacts: Titled 'governor of Judah' (a Persian-appointed provincial administrator) throughout, never 'king' - Judah had no throne at this time.

characters.name: Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest

genealogy.note: Naming collision flag: this Joshua is a different person from Joshua son of Nun, Moses' successor - name only, no relation.

verses.note: Addressed as 'the high priest' alongside Zerubbabel.
Obeys the voice of the LORD along with Zerubbabel and the remnant of the people.
The LORD stirs up his spirit as well, and he joins the temple work.
Told directly, 'be strong, O Joshua, son of Josedech, the high priest... and work: for I am with you.'
Present as the priestly-office holder when Haggai poses the LORD's ceremonial-law question to 'the priests.'

funFacts: Paired with Zerubbabel as joint addressee of every message in the book - civil and religious leadership approached together throughout.

characters.name: The Rebuilding of the House of the LORD
characters.purpose: To reorder the returned exiles' priorities after they let the temple's reconstruction stall while finishing their own houses (1:2-4, 1:9); ties recent drought/crop failure directly to this neglect (1:6, 1:9-11); once work resumes, promises the rebuilt house's glory will exceed the former's (2:7-9) and that from the day the foundation work resumes, the LORD will bless (2:18-19).

verses.note: The people say 'the time is not come' to build, while dwelling in their own 'cieled houses' - the charge that opens the book.
Poor harvests and drought explained as the consequence of the house lying waste while everyone runs to his own house.
Work actually begins on the 24th day of the 6th month.
Compares the modest new foundation to the house's former glory, but promises 'the glory of this latter house shall be greater than of the former,' ending 'in this place will I give peace.'
Marks the day of the temple's (re-)foundation as the turning point for blessing: 'from this day will I bless you.'

characters.name: The Priests' Ruling on Holiness and Defilement
characters.purpose: At the LORD's instruction, Haggai poses two questions to the priests concerning the law: whether holy flesh carried in a garment's skirt sanctifies bread, pottage, wine, oil, or other meat it touches (answered no), and whether one made unclean by touching a dead body defiles those same things by touching them (answered yes, 2:12-13). Applied: 'so is this people, and so is this nation before me... and that which they offer there is unclean' (2:14) - holiness does not spread by mere contact, but uncleanness does, explaining the nation's fruitless labor before the temple work resumed.

verses.note: The LORD instructs Haggai to 'ask now the priests concerning the law' - the two hypothetical questions and the priests' answers ('No' / 'It shall be unclean').
Application: 'so is this people, and so is this nation before me, saith the LORD... and that which they offer there is unclean.'
Recalls earlier crop failures ('smote you with blasting and with mildew and with hail') as consequence, before the temple work resumed.
Marks the same day (the 24th of the 9th month) as the turning point: 'from this day will I bless you.'

characters.name: Darius the king

verses.note: 'In the second year of Darius the king' - opens the book's dating formula; no further description given.
'The second year of Darius the king' - repeated to date the start of the temple work.
'The second year of Darius' - dates the priests'-ruling message.

funFacts: Naming collision flag: at least two other kings named Darius appear elsewhere in scripture (Darius the Mede, Darius the Persian) - conventionally read as different rulers, though this text never draws the distinction itself.

genealogyLists.note: No bulk/unresolved genealogy references in this book - both named human figures beyond the prophet have their father named directly in-text.
